from functools import lru_cache

# The Perrin sequence is defined by its initial conditions
# P(0) = 3, P(1) = 0 and P(2) = 2, together with the recurrence
# P(n) = P(n - 2) + P(n - 3) for n >= 3. Storing the initial
# conditions together makes clear that they are the seed values of
# the definition, from which every other term follows by the
# general recurrence below.
_PERRIN_INITIAL_VALUES = (3, 0, 2)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def get_perrin(n):
    """Return the nth Perrin number using recursion."""
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n must be a non-negative integer")
    if n < len(_PERRIN_INITIAL_VALUES):
        return _PERRIN_INITIAL_VALUES[n]
    return get_perrin(n - 2) + get_perrin(n - 3)
